links.reason: The verse says the thrown trident (விடுசூல) and the body are cut in two by the hurled sword (அயில்வாள்); it never says the thrower is pierced or that a wound is turned back on him. The Kural's smile at a body-spear is not matched, so 'turns the thrown trident on its thrower' is read in.
links.text_issue: sense flagged uncertain; who is pierced and who falls is not in the verse

links.reason: 1744 is a reproach (உண்ணவும் வல்லீர்) and 1731 is a feast; the two make no incompatible claim, they are different scenes in one chapter. Meals as a measure of grief is a theme, not a tension.

Both say two lives became one (ஈருடம் போருயிர் / உயிரொன்றலின்), a real shared formula. But 'the reader knows this union ends' is not in 1981, which gives the cause as never parting; the pairing shows a repeated formula only.

1116 only says Civakan walks bound like a lion by a spider's thread (சிலம்பி நூலாற் சிமிழ்ப்புண்ட). Verse 16 has the god untie the flower-cord; that these are the same binding, and that the thread is 'fulfilled literally', is a reconstruction the verses do not state.

453 praises the eyes as the killing sign of love (கொலைத்தொழில்கொள் வாட்கண்) and NAL 44 rejects eye-as-spear praise (வேலென்று ... கண்ணில்புன் மாக்கள்). The contrast is real, but the note itself says which holds depends on the speaker, so it is a difference of stance, not an incompatible claim.

24 says he took counsel with his mother (தாயொடு எண்ணி) and 1918 opens that counsel, so the link is real; but 1918 holds only the grove setting and 'she speaks' (உரைக்குமிது), and the policy content and its ranking as most compact are not in the verse.
1694 the envoy descends and bows; 1697 the king bids him speak (நீயே உரை). This is plot order, which the graph already holds; 'waits on the king's leave' is not what either verse says.

1339 challenges whether one may stand aside (ஒருவி நிற்றல் உரங்கொல்லோ) and 1341 answers 'let it be, if that is royal custom' (அரச நீதி ஆகிவிடின்); a genuine reply. But 'the rule is made by the debate' overreads a single acceptance.

Both use a small fire / small remainder (எட்டுணைத் தீ; தீயெச்சம்) against an enemy that grows. But the verse says nothing of striking first, and it does state a general law (சிறிதாயினும் விரியப்பெற்றபின் வென்றிடும்), so 'lacks the rule' is false.

2 excuses slips of speech in praise; 17 says a fault in the exalted (the god's stained throat) is still a fault. They are about different things (the poet's words vs the praised one's faults) and no order of the fragments is stated, so the opposition is a reconstruction.

626 rejects கயல் for நீலம்; NAL 44 names குவளை and கயல் as the blind men's praise. A shared vocabulary of eye-similes, nothing more: the attendants do not 'weigh and choose' as a doctrine and no claim conflicts. The unsaid until the last book gain is speculation.

1075 says the base keep conduct from fear (அச்சமே கீழ்களது ஆசாரம்); 1018 says virtue is ashamed of the shameless. Neither denies the other; 1075 is a companion case, and 'looks alike, differs in source' is not drawn from either couplet.

1627 fears she will die (இறந்து படுங்கொலோ) and 1631 answers that her life leaving would take his (உயிர் அய்தி இறக்கும்), so she is unharmed, and adds her Vidyadhara arts. The later verse answers the earlier by argument, as the teaches says.
13 the bird seizes her (பற்றி); 14 it sets her by her father and does not eat the life (பற்றுயிர் உண்ணா). A real reversal, but it is story order and qualifies is a loose label.

1675 opens the spray war (இறைவன்மேல் இனையரானார்); 1678 has the queens cry வென்றனம் and the pool drains. Nothing in either verse is a surrender by the king, so 'the king's surrender is the planned end' is not in the Tamil.

1762 the friends suspect deceit as she does not waste (வாடலொன்றிலள் வஞ்சமாங்கொலோ); 1747 shows her sending Nandattan by a spell. The irony is real but no claim conflicts, and that her calm is 'knowledge' is not stated.

255 lists the effects of a bent sceptre (அரசு கோல் கோடின்: no rain, hunger, chastity breaks) as Dharmadattan's warning to Kattiyangaran; Kural 559 has முறைகோடி ... வானம் பெயல் ஒல்லாது. The epic extends the single effect into a cascade and aims it at seizure of the throne, and the couplet supplies the base rule.

2033 says the pair enjoy desire for long spans like gods (இமையாரின் நுகர்வார்); NAL 16 says youth's joy is fleeting. These speak of heaven-like life and of youth respectively, and the verse itself calls it a shadow, so no incompatible claim is established; the line is hard to construe.

2886 the master-made doll whose pins loosed lose every joint (பொற்பொறி கழல); Siddhar 42 the body as a puppet (பொம்மை) taken up to match the two karmas (இருவினைக்கீடாய்). A real shared body-as-doll image, with different uses; the pairing is moderate, and 2886 itself turns to the prince's leaving.

1074 is only the embrace (தோளாற் தழுவி); the sulk, appeasement and the runners' interruption are in other verses not shown here. The Kural names the triad as love's rewards, so the verse illustrates it, and the claimed narrative cost is not in this unit.

496 has Sitattan say effort can bring a flood of wealth (வெள்ளநிதி வீழும்); Siddhar 641 says wealth came by earlier deeds (முற்றொடர்பிற் செய்த முறைமையால்). A real opposition, but the storm turning him to the second view is not in the packet, and the Siddhar's gain 'an opponent brought round' is unsupported.

167 eyes are poison and nectar at once (நஞ்சும் அமிர்தமுமே) and madden sages; Kural 1091 has two looks, one the sickness and one the cure. The conceit is close, but the Kural's double look is a pain/cure pair, and the epic's 'unseats a king' lies outside the unit.

27 shows Sathanikan giving the throne to Udayanan (பூமிப் பதம் உனக்காக) and leaving; he does not keep his rank, and NAL 21 says kings all die and none is left over (எஞ்சினார் இவ்வுலகத்தில்), which renouncing does not answer. 'Keeps his rank' misdescribes the verse.

Both use rain for giving; Kural 211 calls it a debt (கடப்பாடு) that asks no return, while PN 142 has the rain fall on drained tank and salt land alike (உவர்நிலம் ஊட்டியும்) and calls Pekan's giving கொடைமடம். The poem adds the cost of indiscriminate giving the couplet leaves out.

2261 spares beast, wounded, young and old for the striker's own standing (பிறர்மிச்சில்; மறம் வாடும்); PN 9 the Pandya tells cows, women, the sick to take shelter as the way of dharma (அறத்துஆறு நுவலும்). Both spare the weak, on different grounds; the contrast is real and specific.

2626 shows a youth leaning on a staff and drooling (தண்டூன்றி); NAL 13 has the old leaning on a staff yet clinging to desire. The staff image is shared, but 2626 only says youth does not last (நிலையாதே), not that desire outlives the body, so teaches overreaches.

1660 makes evening a gaping demon with the moon as tooth (வெண்டிங்கள் எயிறிலங்க) come to swallow her; Kural 1221 calls the hour that eats the lives of the wed (உயிருண்ணும் வேலை). The devouring evening is the shared figure and the epic gives it a body.

799 arrows burn the mean-minded kings and warn them off evil in the next body (தீமை இனிக்கொள்ளும் உடம்பினும் துன்னன்மின்); Kural 202 fears evil more than fire because evil yields evil. The verse does not give that ground, and 'the lesser fire' is read in from the couplet.

1395 the friend reads the owl's call as sign he has not left; 1411 Civakan, unrecognised, says he will be seen within ten months (ஐயிரு திங்கள்). Real answer, but the pledge does not mention the omen, so 'omen confirmed' is an inference; verse 1411 is flagged uncertain.

2845 defines knowledge as knowing the real (உணர்தல் ஞானம்), faith as seeing it clearly (தெளிதல் காட்சி) and conduct as holding it; Kural 356 pairs கற்று and கண்டார். The Jain triad adds the third part, so the recipes differ, and both gains are specific.

253 lists friend-betrayal, adultery, rape, flesh-eating and killing a king as minister (அமைச்சனாய் அரசு கொன்றான்); it never mentions ingratitude (செய்ந்நன்றி) or a king who raised him. Ranking regicide as the Kural's unremedied ingratitude is read in.

2096 has even blinking an excess (இமைப்பதும் பெருமிகை) and the burden put down by the king's grace; Kural 345 has the body itself மிகை. The மிகை echo is real but the note misses it, and 'the couplet lays it on the renouncer's own will' is not in the couplet.

33 says fear gains nothing and itself becomes pain and poison-like deeds (அஞ்சுதல் துன்பந்தானே ... நஞ்சென வினைகள்); NAL 33 says the wise take the arrived fruit as old desert. The epic adds fear as a new cause of karma before the fruit, a true extension.

554 has the king say that when the destined time comes none can stop it (பாற்படு காலம் வந்தால் ... விலக்குகிற்பார்); Kural 380 says nothing is stronger than fate. This agrees; the Kural does not see fate 'only as defeating a plan', and the contest is not in the verse.

Both give the elephants as hills and arrows as sparrows (குன்றத்து இறுத்த குரீஇ இனம் போல ... எண்ணருங் குன்றிற் குரீஇயினம்); PN 19 turns to the mothers' grief and Death's flight, KN 8 stays on the spectacle. The shared simile and the differing frames are true.

1552 says no enemy is left (தெவ்வர் அங்கின்மை) and 1381 the Vidyadharas turn back from fate-marked men; that the laughing youth of 1381 is the prince of 1552 is unstated and the marker is unsure of it. A reconstructed link.

698 the lion-shape roars over the Himalaya and Sindhu land; 706 the envoys say a lion lives in the gem hill cave (முழை உறைகின்றது). The verses do not show the envoys are deceived rather than speaking knowingly; the claim that the trick works on them is read in.

376 has Death lay a net (வலையை வைத்தான்) from which only austerity (நோற்று) frees, yet those who know it turn to pleasure; Kural 348 has the renouncers at the head and the rest in the net (வலைப்பட்டார்). The epic adds the net's owner and that knowing is not leaving it.

2060 says heaven's joy comes by austerity yet ends (ஒருநாள் ஈறுடையது) and something is above it (மிசையே); Kural 346 has the one who cuts off 'I' and 'mine' enter a world above the gods'. The epic gives a reason to rank heaven below the goal, and the couplet supplies the means.

245 has the god's promised mantra (என்னை நீர் நினைக்க) recalled and used, and he comes; 244 recalls the god who saved the king on the hunt. A past kindness left a means, so the later verse fulfils the earlier.

NK 36 praises the lord of the vow of non-killing (கொல்லாத நல்விரதக் கோமான்) and SM 1 the one who conquered the sum of deeds (வென்றான் வினையின் தொகை). Both are Jain invocations; but NK 36 names no victory by a vow, so 'victory in the vow of non-killing' is read in and the pairing is the shared theme.
1706 has the moon enter the queen's mouth in union (மதியந்தானே மங்கைதன் செவ்வாய் மடுத்து); 1712 gives the son's birth with cool light (விண் குளிர). An omen of conception and its fulfilment.

23 says the brother came 'by the bidding of a woman' (உதிதற்கு உரியாள் பணியால்) and 1723 says Nandattan came with the word of the peacock-like woman (மயிலனாளால்). The link is real; but the patikam does not name her and 'vision and magical travel' is not in 1723.
